A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HAD-MFC/VAI research, with matching core experiments and readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The changed layout and removal of the NeurIPS checklist do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Battle, Taxi, and Vicsek simulation results in Table 1, vulnerability analyses in Section 5.2, and runtime and perturbation-budget experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds Taxi perturbation-budget results and expanded runtime measurements in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The decomposition, value-learning loss, and greedy/DQN selection framework remain. However, v3 Eq. 12 and Algorithm 2 reverse the selection reward from value-after minus value-before to value-before minus value-after. Algorithm 1 also changes its sampling bound from 1 to 2^(1/p). These are limited revisions to the stated procedure; Algorithm 3 retains the old reward sign, so a consistent implementation-wide correction is not established.

E1.justification: Identifiable results retain Battle, Taxi, and Vicsek; the added Taxi experiments vary budgets and attacker counts within that coverage. However, v1 Appendix C.1 also says Pursuit and an MFC-modified Vicsek variant were tested, without separately identifiable results. v3 omits those statements. The PDFs do not establish whether evaluations were removed or their descriptions were corrected.

E2.justification: Random, DC, Bi-Level RL, PIANO, and RTCA remain in the corresponding attack-performance and Battle-runtime comparisons. The new Taxi sensitivity table uses the same set. New Taxi/Vicsek timing tables include Random and DC but replace no earlier timing comparisons. Expanded PIANO documentation does not establish a changed baseline procedure.

E3.justification: The main benchmark configurations and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. Appendix D.2 adds Taxi settings with 25/50 attackers among 50/100 agents and budgets 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 1.0. Runtime evaluation covers additional configurations, and v3 excludes the one-hour value-function training cost from tabulated timings, whereas v1 explicitly included it as an added term.

E4.justification: Appendix D extends existing perturbation-budget sensitivity analysis from Battle to Taxi and expands computational-cost analysis across configurations and environments. Appendix B adds an unquantified pilot finding that more than 100 cooperative rollouts did not improve performance. The correlation analysis and agent-vulnerability heatmaps are retained; no new component-ablation study appears.

E5.justification: v3 adds uncertainty values to previously point-only Battle runtime and partial-budget results, explicitly describes five-run runtime averages, and introduces Friedman significance tests in Appendix D.2. This does not establish an increase in runs. Main experiments already reported five seeds and uncertainty in v1. Removal of the checklist also removes v1's '95% confidence' statement, leaving v3's uncertainty notation less explicitly defined.

E6.justification: Appendix D substantially expands reported computational-cost and sensitivity results through Taxi/Vicsek runtime tables and new Taxi attack scores. Battle timings also change, such as Random at 64 agents/32 attackers from 1.68 to 1.65 hours. New Taxi results are under added settings, not same-setting improvements over v1. All 126 Table 1 result cells remain identical, and retained Battle sensitivity means differ only in displayed precision.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the backwards generalized-coverage argument with a construction reducing maximum coverage to VAI. Proposition 4.1 and Appendix A.3 change the concentration bound by introducing a 2^(2/p) denominator. Bellman inequalities and optimization signs are revised, Appendix A.4 adds a fixed-Q assumption to its derivation, and Proposition 4.4 is qualified as a first-order interpretation. These substantially revise the mathematical support.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: formulate VAI as HAD-MFC, establish hardness, decouple through a regularized Bellman operator, and select agents through greedy/RL methods while preserving optimal solutions. The main empirical claim of outperforming baselines in 17 of 18 tasks is unchanged.

C2.justification: New Remark 3 distinguishes the claimed exact transformation from neural approximation and suboptimal combinatorial search, while Proposition 4.4 is explicitly framed as post-hoc intuition. Appendix C.2 adds qualifications about PIANO's approximate selection reward and comparison fairness. Appendix D.1 adds a CPU/GPU bottleneck explanation. These refine interpretation and practical qualifications without replacing the central conclusions.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code release; v3 provides a specific repository address. Appendix B newly specifies 100 cooperative rollouts and PGD for the existing minimization step. Appendix D.1 identifies GPU/CPU configurations and within-environment hardware controls, while C.2 clarifies PIANO's final adversarial-policy training. These materially improve reproducibility documentation, although the earlier explicit statement that PIANO uses PPO is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds Liu et al. (2022) on cascading power-grid failures and Madry (2017) for PGD. Positioning relative to mean-field MARL, adversarial attacks, and influence maximization remains substantially unchanged. The switch to author-year citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: The six main sections and Appendices A–D retain their organization. There are targeted rewrites of the abstract, introduction, conclusion, and appendix explanations, plus updated author/correspondence information. v3 adds separate Impact Statement and Acknowledgments sections and removes the NeurIPS checklist, while preserving the overall narrative.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to two-column ICML formatting with a compact author block and substantially rearranged tables and figures. The existing heatmaps and correlation plots exchange figure numbers and locations, with revised captions. Runtime displays expand substantially, new tables are added, and the retained Battle sensitivity table reverses budget-column order and adds uncertainty displays.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability through a correctly directed hardness reduction, additional sensitivity evidence, statistical reporting, and concrete implementation and hardware disclosures. The gains remain limited by incomplete mathematical corrections: Algorithm 3 retains the old reward sign, and Appendix A.5 retains an operator sign inconsistent with the revised main text. Losing the earlier confidence-level description also weakens uncertainty clarity. Overall, the clearer documentation and supporting evidence provide a modest net quality improvement.
